faqs.question: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit in retail, and how can margins be protected?

description: A battle-tested execution framework covering every step from idea to scale, tailored for Indian market realities.
Eliminates confusion and saves months of costly mistakes whether starting from a home kitchen or planning a small manufacturing unit.
Provides guidance across costing, licensing, operations, marketing, growth, and risk management in the Indian food industry.
learningHighlights: Understand the 5 stages of food business execution: Idea Validation, Business Setup, Launch & Sales, Systemize Operations, and Scale & Grow
Identify and navigate essential compliance and legal requirements including FSSAI (Basic, State, Central), GST, and local licenses
Calculate product selling prices, understand major cost heads, and protect gross margins between 40-60%
Source reliable suppliers, establish backups, and evaluate wholesale mandis vs. online B2B platforms
Implement daily operational checklists, quality control protocols, and FIFO inventory management
Deploy low-cost marketing via WhatsApp Business, Google My Business, social media, and food delivery aggregators
Evaluate funding options including self-funding and government schemes like PMEGP, MUDRA, Stand-Up India, and PMFME
audience: Beginner entrepreneurs testing food ideas with minimal investment
Aspiring cloud kitchen and packaged food business owners
Small manufacturing and catering entrepreneurs looking to scale

faqs.question: Which FSSAI license is needed when starting a home-based food business?
faqs.answer: A Basic FSSAI registration is suitable for home-based businesses with an annual turnover below ₹12 lakh and costs ₹100.

faqs.question: What gross and net profit margins should a food business aim for?
faqs.answer: A food business should aim for a gross margin of 40-60% and a net profit margin of 10-20% after all expenses.

faqs.question: When is GST registration mandatory for a food business in India?
faqs.answer: GST registration is mandatory if turnover exceeds ₹40 lakh (₹20 lakh in special states), if selling across state borders, or if selling on e-commerce platforms.
